title: Counting to Ten
logline: During harvest, a grain measurer fills basket after basket by hand, calling each count aloud, never rushing and never losing the place.

object.note: Object 7 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: The long night's struggle to stay upright gives way to a harvest day kept steady by counting aloud, basket after basket, never losing the place.

thread_out.thread: From grain in the hands to clay in the hands: a potter's family reading hardness, wetness, warmth and air long before any of it has a name.

lesson.in_simple_terms: A simple count, neither rushed nor dragged, can keep attention steady through a long day. The old meditation texts use a grain measurer calling out each measure as their picture for counting the breath.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: ඉක්මන් නොකර, පමා නොකර කරන සරල ගණන් කිරීමකින් සිත එක තැනක රඳවා ගත හැකි බවත්, ආනාපානසතියේ හුස්ම ගණන් කිරීමට පොත් උපමාවක් ලෙස ගන්නේ වී මනින්නාගේ ගණන බවත් මෙයින් පෙනේ.
lesson.the_teaching: In mindfulness of breathing, the texts begin with counting: not below five and not beyond ten, then starting again from one, while letting the breath run naturally rather than forcing it. The first, slow counting is compared to a paddy measurer who fills each measure, removes the rubbish and calls the number, and the count is said to steady the mind the way a pole holds a boat against a current. Behind the working body, the four origins of matter are at work too: mind-born matter moves the limbs, and where food-born matter does not arise, growth and the strength to work weaken.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The film stays with the measurer's rhythm: the measure filled and levelled, straw and stones flicked out, each number called aloud hour after hour while farmers watch a tally that decides their season. The viewer can hear the count carrying a body through heat and fatigue, and notice when the rhythm holds and when it slips, without anyone mentioning breath.

key_terms.en: mindfulness of breathing in and out

lesson.caution: This is not breath control or a quick relaxation trick: the texts warn against forcing the breath and set counting inside a long, guided practice aimed at more than calm.
lesson.builds_on: Where the watchman's body sagged as attention faded, this film shows the other side: a plain, steady count keeping attention, and with it a working body, in one place.
